changelog: The score arrives. This build is almost entirely music: thirteen beds, written as one piece of work, replacing the previous set wholesale rather than joining it. That replacement is the point rather than a side effect. Every bed shares a tonic, which is what lets any of them crossfade into any other without a lurch — and that only holds if they all come from the same score. Mixing the old files in would have broken the property the whole thing is built on. What you'll hear that you didn't before The camp and the outpost have their own music. Previously the map sent every "safe" location to a single cue. The camp is a low jazz trio; the outpost is an upbeat F# major. The old `safe` bed stayed behind for the run summary, which is neither of those places. Battle and boss are now opposites rather than loud and louder. Battle is 135 BPM F# aeolian over a marching snare. Boss is 104 BPM F# phrygian with no snare anywhere. One note apart, so they still crossfade cleanly — but you will never mistake one for the other. The campaign escalates by instrument, not by volume. It used to be one colour layer that got louder each act. Now three layers stack: act I is the bed alone, act III adds two fronts plus encirclement, act IV brings all three. A new instrument arriving reads as escalation in a way that turning one up never quite did. Under the hood The files are rendered straight to AAC from the same 24-bit master, so the game gets one lossy generation instead of an MP3 transcoded into AAC. Null-tested against the approved master at 0.998 correlation with zero sample lag. The download grew about 13 MB. That is the score, and it is the only reason. Everything else No gameplay changes. The Daily Commission fixes from 0.0.58–0.0.60 — Resume no longer destroying the run it offers to continue, one attempt per Commission, readable run modifiers — are all unchanged and still in place.
